questions.question: You will be working with a patient who has had a STROKE. Which of the following description can best characterize the typical gait pattern of the patient?
options: A. A shift of the trunk to the affected side with weight bearing
B. Weight shift to the unaffected side with circumduction of the affected leg
C. Excessive anterior tilt and lumbar lordosis with exaggerated arm swing
D. Excessive upper extremity held in extension and excessive lower extremity held in flexion
questions.answer: B. Weight shift to the unaffected side with circumduction of the affected leg

questions.question: Mr. Tan suffered from a stroke and he couldn’t walk. According to the classification of the World Health Organization (WHO), his inability to move his left ankle joint is:
options: A. An impairment
B. A handicap
C. A disability
D. All of the above
questions.answer: A. An impairment

questions.question: Consider the following statements about the goal of upper-limb rehabilitation. 1. Reduce spasticity 2. Reduce neuroplasticity to improve patients’ motor function 3. Inhibit atypical muscle synergies 4. Allows the healthy limb to do every daily task Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
options: A. II only
B. I, III, and IV only
C. I and III only
D. All of the three
questions.answer: C. I and III only

questions.question: Consider the following statements about rehabilitation robots. I. Robot-assisted therapy can provide high-intensity training for stroke patients II. Robot-assisted therapy will cause the physical strain on patients III. Robots can achieve the range of motion exercise and strengthening training IV. Robots can combine with Virtual-Reality system to deliver the activities of daily living training Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
options: A. I and III only
B. All of the three
C. I, III, and IV only
D. II only
questions.answer: C. I, III, and IV only

questions.question: Consider the following description about an actuating method. I. It has an internal bladder II. It has a braided mesh shell with flexible but non-extensible threads III. Its length can be controlled by compressed air Which actuating method(s) is/are mentioned with the above description?
options: A. Pneumatic Artificial Muscle only
B. Electric motor only
C. Hydraulic actuator only
D. Pneumatic and hydraulic actuator
questions.answer: A. Pneumatic Artificial Muscle only

questions.question: Neuroplasticity is the basis for rehabilitation therapy for stroke. Neuroplasticity means:
options: A. New brain cells can grow in response to therapy training
B. Brain motor areas damaged in stroke can be recovered in response to therapy training
C. Brain motor areas which are “not used” can be activated to take over motor control functions if properly stimulated
D. Brain motor areas are soft can be deformed by therapy training
questions.answer: C. Brain motor areas which are “not used” can be activated to take over motor control functions if properly stimulated

questions.question: A patient with hemiparesis after stroke will have
options: A. Paralysis of the two upper limbs
B. Muscular weakness or partial paralysis restricted to one side of the body
C. Paralysis of the two lower limbs
D. Paralysis of the left arm and right leg
questions.answer: B. Muscular weakness or partial paralysis restricted to one side of the body

questions.question: Ischemic stroke is caused by:
options: A. Disrupted blood supply due to rupture blood vessel in the brain
B. Reduced blood supply due to blockage in blood vessel in the brain
C. Injury of the brain due to external forces
D. Tumor in the brain
questions.answer: B. Reduced blood supply due to blockage in blood vessel in the brain

questions.question: The control system of a rehabilitation robot usually has 3 levels: high level, med level, and low level; the low level control handles the following
options: A. Detect the use movement intent
B. Determine whether to use passive control mode or active control mode
C. All of the statements are true
D. Controlling the accurate force output of the actuators for the joints
questions.answer: D. Controlling the accurate force output of the actuators for the joints

questions.question: You are a rehabilitation engineer, your role could include the following
options: A. Provide financial tips to the family of the patient
B. Test the performance of the prosthetic leg for the patient
C. Massage the legs of the patient
D. Measuring the vital signs of the patient
questions.answer: B. Test the performance of the prosthetic leg for the patient

questions.question: Which of the statements is true about end effector based upper limb rehabilitation robot?
options: A. It is only targeted the chronic stage of the rehabilitation process
B. It is attached to the distal part of the upper limb
C. It is only useful for hand rehabilitation
D. It can be attached to only one limb
questions.answer: B. It is attached to the distal part of the upper limb

questions.question: Your patient has a SCI at cervical level, with residual head movements. Can this patient control a robotic arm with 6 DOFs?
options: A. Yes, with an indirect interface with a scanning mechanism
B. Yes, but only 1-2 DOFs of the arm
C. Yes, with an indirect interface with a caregiver's mediation
D. No, because the patient cannot control 6 different inputs
questions.answer: A. Yes, with an indirect interface with a scanning mechanism

questions.question: Your patient is a teen ager with cerebral palsy and not accurate control of hand and finger movements. How to enable your patient to type?
options: A. Pedal-activated scanning keyboard
B. Scanning keyboard with two switches: one for scanning the keys and one for selecting the chosen key
C. Restricted keyboard usable with finger movements and no need for hand movements
D. Enlarged keyboard with keys large enough for the patient's accuracy
E. Scanning keyboard with pre-set scanning time and one switch for key selection
questions.answer: D. Enlarged keyboard with keys large enough for the patient's accuracy

questions.question: Is this an interface to an assistive device with selection set >2?
options: A. True
B. False
questions.answer: A. True
questions.verificationRisk: image-dependent; unverifiable from extracted text alone

questions.question: Wheelchair-mounted manipulators
options: A. need to be used in the same place
B. need to be teleoperated by the user
C. are easy to use because preprogrammed
questions.answer: B. need to be teleoperated by the user

questions.question: Assistive mobile robots
options: A. require autonomous navigation and manipulation
B. are easy to program because the environment is structured
C. need to teleoperated by the user
questions.answer: A. require autonomous navigation and manipulation

questions.question: Which of the following robotic technologies can contribute to assistive technologies?
options: A. Automation
B. Exoskeletons
C. Manufacturing
D. Navigation
questions.answer: D. Navigation

questions.question: Auntie Katherine is 83-year old and hemiplegic from a stroke. She has a full-time caregiver. Is she an ideal user of robotic assistive technology?
options: A. True
B. False
questions.answer: B. False

questions.question: Target users of manipulation aids
options: A. upper-limb amputee
B. quadriplegic
C. lower-limb amputee
D. paraplegic
questions.answer: B. quadriplegic

questions.question: What robotic functions in a smart wheelchair?
options: A. Autonomous manipulation
B. Localization and mapping
C. Autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance
D. Shared-control navigation and obstacle avoidance
E. Wheelchair motor control
questions.answer: D. Shared-control navigation and obstacle avoidance

questions.question: Your user is a young tetraplegic with reduced upper limb functioning. What wheelchair is best suited?
options: A. Smart wheelchair
B. Manual wheelchair
C. Power-assist wheelchair
D. Power wheelchair
questions.answer: A. Smart wheelchair

questions.question: Possible shared control of smart wheelchairs:
options: A. The user sets heading and the smart wheelchair ensures collision avoidance
B. The user controls speed and avoids obstacles
C. The smart wheelchair sets heading and the user controls speed
questions.answer: A. The user sets heading and the smart wheelchair ensures collision avoidance

questions.question: Maria is paraplegic and leaves on the 3rd floor of an old building with no elevator. Does she have
options: A. An impairment, but no limitation of activity, nor restriction of participation
B. An impairment, limitation of activity and restriction of participation
C. No impairment, but limitation of activity
D. No limitation of activity, but restriction of participation
E. An impairment and limitation of activity, but no restriction of participation
questions.answer: B. An impairment, limitation of activity and restriction of participation

questions.question: Maria is paraplegic and leaves on the 13th floor of a condo with elevator. Does she have
options: A. An impairment, limitation of activity and restriction of participation
B. No impairment, but limitation of activity
C. An impairment and limitation of activity, but no restriction of participation
D. No limitation of activity, but restriction of participation
E. An impairment, but no limitation of activity, nor restriction of participation
questions.answer: C. An impairment and limitation of activity, but no restriction of participation

questions.question: Possible sensors on a smart wheelchair
options: A. Infrared sensors
B. Force sensors
C. IMU
D. Ultrasound sensors
E. Hall-effect sensors
